newsitem.title: GREECE: OLYMPICS-ATHENS 2004 BID LAUNCHES SPONSORSHIP PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ATHENS 2004 BID LAUNCHES SPONSORSHIP PROGRAMME.

text.p: Greece launched a sponsorship programme on Wednesday to help fund a bid by Athens to host the 2004 Olympic Games, bidding committee officials said.

"The contribution of the business world to our effort will be very important. Their funding is an investment in our capabilities to go beyond Greek borders. The 2004 Games is a bet with our future, a great chance for Greece," bid committee president Yanna Angelopoulou said.
The bid committee set six categories of sponsors with sums ranging from $1.2 million to $100,000.
Angelopoulou and her husband, steel works and shipping tycoon Theodore Angelopoulos, were named the first major "benefactors" with an offer around $2.5 million.
The benefactors will have the right to use the Athens bid logo on their products and participate in all activities of the bid committee.
"Our team of sponsors will give a clear message abroad that the elite of the busiuness world backs the Athens bid," Greek Olympic Committee vice-president Marton Simitchek said.

Athens is among 11 candidates for the 2004 Games and is considered among the favourites, along with Cape Town, Stockholm and Rome. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) will produce a short-list of four or five in March before making its final choice in September.

After losing the Centenary 1996 Games to Atlanta, Athens vowed never to bid again. But it changed its mind and decided to challenge for the 2004 Olympics by projecting an image of a modern city with state-of-the-art facilities.
